However, no transformer easement boundaries are depicted on any sheet, and no easement widths or dimensions are specified.
agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement applies to all sites and requires transformer easements to be shown around pads with widths determined by AE Design for accessibility. The phrase 'Additional electric easements may be required at a later date' on Sheet 9 indicates that easements are recognized as a requirement but not yet depicted or detailed. The electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pads without any associated easement boundaries. This is a deficiency—applicant must work with AE Design to establish and depict transformer easements.

applicableAreas: All transformer pads shown on Sheet 21
findings.comment: Applicant must: (1) coordinate with Austin Energy Design to determine the required transformer easement width for each pad, (2) depict transformer easement boundaries (not just note 'additional easements may be required') on the site plan and electrical plan, (3) document easement width in plan notes, and (4) ensure easement boundaries are not in conflict with recorded property easements or other site features.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 21 (electrical plan) shows transformer pad locations and underground electric lines. However, no documentation explicitly traces the electrical routing path from each transformer to its associated meter to confirm that 100% of the routing is on private property. The electrical notes on Sheet 21 mention contractor verification of utility locations but do not document the property status of the electrical routing.
agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement applies to all sites and requires electrical routing from transformer to meter to be 100% on private property. While Sheet 21 shows both transformers and meters, no documented analysis or dimension table confirms the property status of the entire electrical routing path. Without explicit documentation that all conduit, cable, and connections from each transformer to each meter are located entirely on private property (not in public right-of-way), compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Electrical routing from all transformer pads to associated meters
findings.comment: Provide notation on electrical plan confirming that 100% of electrical routing from each transformer pad to its associated meter(s) is located on private property, with no portion in public right-of-way. Include cross-reference to property boundaries from site plan (Sheet 9) and plat (Sheet 2).

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 21 (electrical plan) shows 4 transformer pads represented by simple rectangular symbols with no dimensions (length × width). Vision analysis confirmed 'There are no numerical dimensions (length x width) provided for the transformer pads on this specific sheet.' No references to AE Design-approved transformer pad detail sheets are provided on the electrical plan or on any of the construction detail sheets (Sheets 22-28).
agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement applies to all sites and requires transformer pad dimensions to match AE Design-approved specifications for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase). The electrical plan shows generic transformer pad symbols without dimensions and without reference to AE Design detail sheets. The grouping guidance specifically notes 'Specific pad dimensions are determined by Austin Energy Design on a project-specific basis, not standardized in code.' The absence of both pad dimensions and reference to AE Design specifications is a deficiency.

applicableAreas: All transformer pads shown on Sheet 21
findings.comment: Applicant must: (1) obtain Austin Energy Design approval documents and transformer pad detail sheets for each of the 4 transformer pads, (2) confirm the service type (single-phase or three-phase) for each pad and the associated electrical load, (3) depict the AE Design-approved pad dimensions (length × width) on the electrical plan for each pad, and (4) provide the approved detail sheets as part of the plan set (reference from electrical plan detail callouts).

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 10 (fire protection plan) shows parking areas and fire lanes with 24'-26' widths. Sheet 21 (electrical plan) shows 4 transformer pads at various locations. However, no dimension callouts document the distances from transformer pads to parking areas or drive lanes, and no bollard details or specifications are provided on any sheet.
agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement applies only when transformer pads are located within 4 feet of parking areas, drive aisles, or vehicle circulation routes. Vision analysis of both sheets does not clearly establish specific parking stall locations adjacent to transformer pads with measured distances. However, without dimensioned measurements showing distances from each pad to the nearest parking/circulation area, and without specifications showing whether bollards are present (and if required, whether they are 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts correctly spaced to allow equipment door opening), compliance cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: All transformer pads relative to parking areas and drive lanes
findings.comment: Applicant must: (1) provide dimensioned measurements on electrical plan showing distance from each transformer pad to nearest parking stall or vehicle circulation route, (2) for any pad within 4 feet of parking/circulation areas, provide bollard details referencing AE Design equipment pad specifications showing: 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts, spacing that allows equipment door opening, and installation details, or (3) if no bollards are required, document that all pads are more than 4 feet from parking/vehicle areas.

agentTrace.observation: Facts.md does not indicate overhead distribution facilities serving the site. Sheet 21 (electrical plan) shows underground electric lines. No overhead distribution conductors, poles, or associated customer infrastructure (buildings, parking garages, light poles, signs, antennas, tanks) are shown constructed under or over overhead distribution lines.
agentTrace.reasoning: This requirement applies only when overhead distribution facilities are present. The site appears to use underground electrical distribution based on Sheet 21. Without evidence of overhead distribution facilities on adjacent properties or adjacent street frontage, and without any indication that customer structures are being installed under such lines, this requirement does not appear to apply to this project.

findings.comment: If overhead distribution facilities exist on adjacent properties or streets, confirm through site plan and utility notes that no customer buildings, parking garages, structures, poles, signs, antennas, tanks, or other facilities are installed under or over overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors.
